chunks: From him, from Ibn Fadhdhal, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Let your seeking of livelihood be above the earning of the squanderer and below the seeking of the greedy one who is pleased with his world and reliant upon it; but rather, descend yourself from that to the station of the equitable and self-restrained one. Raise yourself above the station of the neglectful and the weak, and earn what is inevitable from it.
Indeed, those who are given wealth and then are not grateful — there is no wealth for them.

key_terms.الْحَرِيصُ: The greedy — one who is excessively desirous of worldly gain
key_terms.الْمَعِيشَةُ: Livelihood — the means of sustaining life, used in Shia ethics to denote both material provision and its spiritual dimensions
key_terms.الْمُضَيِّعُ: The squanderer — one who wastes resources and opportunities through negligence
key_terms.الْمُنْصِفُ الْمُتَعَفِّفُ: The equitable and self-restrained — the ideal middle position characterized by justice and chastity of desire

ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about the proper attitude toward seeking a livelihood?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prescribes a middle path in earning one's livelihood: one must work harder than the negligent person who squanders opportunities, yet not become enslaved to worldly greed like one who clings to the material world. The teaching was addressed to his followers navigating the complex economy of early Abbasid Iraq, where both passive poverty and obsessive wealth accumulation were spiritual dangers. The concluding statement that ingratitude strips the blessing of wealth reflects the classical Shia ethical framework in which divine blessings are contingent upon gratitude.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Ibn Fazaal, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Let your seeking of the livelihood be above the earning of the squanderer and below the seeking of the greedy one the one pleased with his world and reliant upon it, but descend yourself from that to be at the status of the equitable ones, the conservative. Raise yourself from the status of the neglectful, the weak, and earn what is inevitable from it.
Those who are Granted the wealth, then are not grateful, there is no wealth for them’.
en.sarwar: 8. It is narrated from him (narrator of previous Hadith) from ibn Faddal from the one whom he has mentioned who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

your effort in work for living must be above the efforts of a losing person and below that of a greedy one who is happy with confidence in the worldly matters. You must keep your soul in the position of the fair and conservatives ones, and lift your soul above the position of neglectful and weak ones. You must earn what is necessary.
Those who are granted wealth but do not appreciate it they, in fact, have no wealth at all.’”
